typed_core.name: financial_institution_name
typed_core.why: AS-2 (rule reads it) — identifies the account the debit came from; must be a verified borrower account

typed_core.name: account_owner_names
typed_core.why: AS-2 — the account must be the borrower's, 'not an undisclosed source'; flattened person[] -> primary + _2 + _count

typed_core.name: account_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII (registered masked) — the account key AS-2 uses to confirm the debit left a verified account
typed_core.prompt_hint: Mask the account number to last-4

typed_core.name: statement_period_start
typed_core.why: context/recency — flattened from statement_period date_range; frames the debit's timeframe

typed_core.name: statement_period_end
typed_core.why: context/recency — the other half of the flattened statement_period

typed_core.name: transaction_date
typed_core.why: AS-2 — the debit date; must fall within the sourcing timeframe relative to the contract

typed_core.name: posting_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator for transaction_date — the cleared/posted date can differ from the transaction date (degraded from date)

typed_core.name: withdrawal_amount
typed_core.why: AS-2 — the debit amount matched against the contract EMD

typed_core.name: transaction_type
typed_core.why: AS-2 — debit / wire / check / ACH; how the EMD left the account

typed_core.name: payee_or_recipient
typed_core.why: AS-2 — the funds must go to escrow/title/seller, not an undisclosed party

typed_core.name: check_number
typed_core.why: disambiguator/evidence — ties the debit to a cancelled check

typed_core.name: wire_ach_trace_number
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — ties the debit to a wire/ACH; promote so it is masked, not left unmasked in the catch-all

typed_core.name: transaction_description
typed_core.why: processor — the memo (may read 'EMD'/'escrow deposit'); corroborates purpose

typed_core.name: balance_after_transaction
typed_core.why: processor — shows the account held the funds; sufficiency context

typed_core.name: check_cleared_or_transaction_completed
typed_core.why: AS-2 — 'fire if unshown': confirms the debit actually cleared, not just initiated

typed_core.name: related_emd_receipt_reference
typed_core.why: reconciliation — escrow/title receipt reference to tie the debit to the EMD receipt

typed_core.name: related_purchase_contract_amount
typed_core.why: AS-2 — the contract EMD amount this debit is matched against

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity/linkage — links the EMD to the subject transaction

rejected.reason: a debit proof does not have effective/expiry; transaction_date is the event date

rejected.reason: not on an EMD debit proof

rejected.name: signature_blocks
rejected.reason: a cancelled check's endorsement is on the reverse; captured via check_front_and_back_available flag, marginal — catch-all

rejected.name: check_front_and_back_available
rejected.reason: evidence-completeness flag; marginal, no AS-2 gate; catch-all

encoding_variations: transaction_type — no enum coercer; 'Withdrawal', 'Debit', 'Wire Out', 'Online Transfer', 'Check', 'ACH Debit'. Degrade to str
transaction_date vs posting_date — statements print one or both; a wire confirmation prints a value date; a cancelled check prints the paid date. Keep both so a timeframe test uses the right one
check_number vs wire_ach_trace_number — mutually exclusive by instrument (check vs wire/ACH); which one is present is itself evidence of the payment rail
withdrawal_amount — with $/commas/parentheses (a debit may show as (10,000.00) or -10,000.00); parsed to Decimal
check_cleared_or_transaction_completed — 'Cleared', 'Posted', 'Paid', 'Completed' vs 'Pending'. Degrade the boolean to str

open_questions.q: statement_period date_range flattening — there is no date_range coercer; flattened to statement_period_start/_end
open_questions.recommendation: two dates, so a timeframe test can compare

open_questions.q: related_purchase_contract_amount presence — the contract EMD amount is often NOT restated on the debit proof (it lives on the purchase agreement); AS-2 already cross-reads the contract
options: keep the field for when it is restated
drop it and always read the contract
open_questions.recommendation: (a) — capturing it when present lets AS-2 match in one place and flags contract-vs-proof mismatches

open_questions.q: Wire trace as PII — wire_ach_trace_number is restricted
open_questions.recommendation: confirm registration (pre_masked false) so it is masked at the snapshot rather than stored raw in the catch-all GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

open_questions.q: Cancelled-check image — when the proof is a check image, front/back availability and the endorsement carry authenticity signal but no AS-2 field
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the catch-all is acceptable for those

notes: No existing_extractor for this document type — new schema.

18 typed-core rows. AS-2 keys on withdrawal_amount + transaction_date + account identity/ownership + payee + cleared-flag + the contract amount to match; the rest are disambiguators and reconciliation. Within range for a one-rule (but active/NOW) document.

This document proves the earnest money LEFT the borrower's account — the three common forms are a bank-statement line showing the debit, a cancelled check (front/back), or a wire/ACH confirmation. If the proof is a full bank statement, the transaction list belongs to the bank_statement schema, not here.

PII: account_number_masked already in _PII_FIELDS (pre_masked true); wire_ach_trace_number needs _PII_FIELDS registration pre_masked false (restricted; otherwise lands unmasked in the catch-all). transaction_description is not itself a PII field, but free-text memos can carry names/partial account numbers; note for the redactor (the transaction-description pattern). account_owner_names are person names at standard sensitivity (identity).

posting_date is typed str with a '(date)' annotation in the doc — recorded as degraded_from 'date' (kept as str rather than a coerced date); flagged as ambiguity because degrading a coercer-eligible date to str is unusual.
